articles.title: Search is on for 4 adults and 2 children after plane crashes off Mississippi coast
articles.summary: Dunes are seen at Horn Island on August 26, 2026.  - Austin Steele/CNN Authorities are searching for six people after a plane crashed into the water northeast of Horn Island, Mississippi , on Tuesday afternoon, the US Coast Guard said. There were four adults and two children aboard the Cessna Centurion 210 aircraft, according to the agency. The US Coast Guard received a call around 3:45 p.m. Tuesday after the FAA lost communication with the aircraft, a spokesperson for the US Coast Guard Mobile told CNN. Crews searching the scene have so far found three life jackets, a life raft and the cabin of the aircraft, the spokesperson added. Flight tracking data shows the Cessna 210 was flying from New Orleans to Fort Myers, Florida. About 30 minutes after take off, while it was at about 8,800 feet in the air, just south of Pascagoula, Mississippi, the plane suddenly plunged toward the water, according to the website Flightradar24. The aircraft was diving at 18,000 feet a minute, more than 200 miles per hour, in the final seconds before the tracking data ceases. Birds fly along the shore at Horn Island on August 26, 2026.  - Austin Steele/CNN The National Transportation Safety Board will lead the investigation into the crash, according to the Federal Aviation Administration, which will also be assisting in the probe. The US Coast Guard is on scene along with the Mississippi Department of Marine Resources and local agencies. Horn Island is a remote, undeveloped island about 12 nautical miles from Biloxi, Mississippi, that is only accessible by private boat. The journey from nearby Biloxi, Ocean Springs or Pascagoula takes about 30 minutes to an hour. The island is part of the Gulf Islands National Seashore, a national park that includes a dozen islands stretching 160 miles across Mississippi and Florida. Horn Island is about 10 miles long and only about a mile wide. It is a popular summer destination for state residents. This story has been updated with additional information. CNN’s Alisha Ebrahimji contributed to this report. articles.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia flying to Spain after months of U.S. deportation efforts
articles.summary: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the El Salvador native who was mistakenly deported last year and sent to a notorious prison in his home country, is planning to leave the U.S. for Spain on Tuesday, according to multiple U.S. officials familiar with the matter. Abrego Garcia, whose case became an early flashpoint in the debate over the Trump administration's deportation crackdown, is set to fly to Spain on a commercial flight Tuesday, according to the sources, who requested anonymity to talk about an arrangement that has not been disclosed publicly. The exact nature of his arrangements and the conditions of his departure from the U.S. were not immediately clear. But the federal judge in Maryland overseeing his civil legal case issued an order Friday that remains sealed. CBS News has reached out to an attorney and representatives for Abrego Garcia. The move by Abrego Garcia comes after the Trump administration spent months trying to deport the man, who came to the U.S. illegally 15 years ago and had been living in Maryland with his wife and children when he was detained by immigration authorities in March 2025. He was then deported to El Salvador and held for months in the country's CECOT prison, despite a previous court order barring him from being sent back to his home country. He was brought back to the United States last year to face criminal charges. Abrego Garcia has maintained for more than a year that if he had to leave the U.S. again, he would be willing to go to Costa Rica, and designated the Central American nation as his preferred country of removal. But the Trump administration had resisted that suggestion and instead unsuccessfully sought to deport Abrego Garcia to numerous African countries, including Uganda, Eswatini and Ghana. In more recent months, the Department of Homeland Security said it was ready to deport Abrego Garcia to Liberia — part of a broader practice of sending deportees to countries in Africa. Abrego Garcia's departure from the U.S. came weeks after a hearing before U.S. District Judge Paula Xinis, who has been presiding over a civil case stemming from his deportation last year, was abruptly cancelled . The judge ordered Immigration and Customs Enforcement last year to release Abrego Garcia from immigration custody and has continued to bar immigration authorities from detaining him while litigation continued. But the Trump administration had sought to lift Xinis' orders, which it said were the only impediments to Abrego Garcia's "prompt removal." The Justice Department said in March that the government was "ready, willing, and able" to deport Abrego Garcia to Liberia in West Africa. Abrego Garcia's case gained national prominence last year after a top administration official acknowledged that his removal to El Salvador was an "error." Following his arrest by immigration authorities in March 2025, Abrego Garcia was among the more than 200 immigrants who were sent to El Salvador and detained at its notorious supermax prison, the Terrorism Confinement Center, or CECOT. But Abrego Garcia had been granted a withholding of removal by an immigration judge in 2019, which prevented immigration authorities from deporting him to his home country of El Salvador because he was at risk of persecution by local gangs. In April 2025, Xinis ordered the Department of Homeland Security to bring Abrego Garcia back to the U.S., and the Supreme Court said the government had to facilitate his release from Salvadoran custody. The Trump administration ultimately brought Abrego Garcia back to the U.S. in June 2025, but only after he was indicted on federal charges of human smuggling stemming from a 2022 traffic stop in Tennessee. Abrego Garcia pleaded not guilty and in May, a federal judge in Tennessee dismissed the criminal charges on the grounds that his prosecution was vindictive. The Justice Department has appealed that decision , and arguments before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 6th Circuit are scheduled for February. articles.title: Chinese tech giant convicted in sweeping U.S. criminal case over its business in Iran
articles.summary: By Karen Freifeld NEW YORK, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei was convicted by a jury in New York City on Tuesday in a sprawling US criminal case on charges that it deceived banks about its business in Iran and stole trade secrets from American companies. The verdict came ‌in a criminal case that began in 2018, with the US government the following year placing Huawei on a trade blacklist that restricted its access ‌to US technology amid American concerns that Huawei posed national security risks. The jury in Brooklyn federal court found Huawei guilty on 10 of the 12 criminal counts the company faced, including bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions ​violations and conspiring to steal trade secrets. The jury acquitted Huawei of conspiring to obstruct justice and racketeering conspiracy, a charge alleging the company had acted as a criminal enterprise. The trial lasted more than two months, with prosecutors calling more than 60 witnesses and the defense calling 15. It was not immediately clear what penalties Huawei will face when US District Judge Ann Donnelly sentences it on September 14, 2027. Reuters stories in 2012 and 2013 helped expose Huawei's activities in Iran and were discussed during the trial. "After the media started questioning Huawei's operations in ‌Iran, so did Huawei's banks," prosecutor Meredith Arfa told jurors during ⁠closing arguments in the case last week. Brian Heberlig, a lawyer for Huawei, said the company was disappointed by the convictions but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge vindicated its "good-faith compliance culture." "We fully expect to appeal," Heberlig told reporters. US Attorney Joseph Nocella said in a ⁠statement: “Few crimes are as serious as Huawei’s decades-long pattern of endangering US national security, violating the sanctity of US commerce, and impeding the enforcement of US laws.” China's embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Asked how much the company may have to pay in penalties, Heberlig said it was premature to comment, but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge could make ​a ​significant difference. Experts have said the case did not undermine Huawei's business, as the company diversified and emerged ​as a key player in China's push for artificial intelligence. FOUNDER'S DAUGHTER ‌WAS DETAINED In December 2018, Meng Wanzhou, Huawei's chief financial officer and daughter of the company's founder, was detained in Canada on a US warrant, prompting a diplomatic crisis involving the United States, China and Canada. Meng had been secretly indicted on US charges of misleading an HSBC banker about Huawei's business in Iran, so the company could move dollars in and out of Iran in violation of American sanctions. Meng fought extradition to the US for nearly three years, before entering a deferred prosecution agreement and flying home to China to a hero's welcome. The charges against her were dropped. Meng did not testify at trial, though an HSBC banker she met with in 2013 did testify. The 2018 indictment alleged that Huawei misled ‌HSBC, Standard Chartered and BNP Paribas about its business dealings in Iran. Prosecutors added new charges ​in 2020, including allegations that Huawei conspired to steal trade secrets from US technology companies over two decades. THE ​PROSECUTION CASE During the trial, prosecutors sought to prove that Huawei stole source code from ​Cisco Systems for its routers, stole wireless telecommunications company Quintel's antenna technology, and hired a professor to gain access to a circuit board developed by ‌semiconductor company CNEX. Jurors watched a video that, according to prosecutors, showed a Huawei ​employee slipping a piece of a T-Mobile ​testing robot into his backpack, and heard about a Huawei engineer sneaking into a Fujitsu booth at a trade show to photograph a device. Prosecutors gave jurors a statement attached to Meng's deferred prosecution agreement in which she acknowledged that the company illegally conducted business in Iran. The defense argued that HSBC and the other banks ​knew about Huawei's business in Iran and were competing for ‌Huawei's business. Heberlig accused prosecutors during his closing argument of having "cherry-picked" a handful of disparate incidents to support their claim of a 20-year conspiracy. Heberlig said ​Huawei succeeded through "hard work, innovation, and investment in research and development." The company has more than 200,000 employees and operates in approximately 170 countries. (Additional reporting ​by Luc Cohen and Jonathan Stempel; Editing by Jonathan Spicer, Noeleen Walder and Will Dunham) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/chinas-huawei-convicted-us-criminal-201624138.html

articles.title: 81.5 million Americans expected to travel as Thanksgiving storms threaten both coasts
articles.summary: Millions of Americans hitting the road and skies for Thanksgiving could run into storms on both coasts, including one that could last through Thanksgiving Day. Record-challenging king tides are forecast on both coasts, threatening coastal flooding from California to Florida. "A strong coastal storm will bring heavy rain, strong winds, and instances of coastal flooding for much of the East Coast during Thanksgiving," according to a Tuesday afternoon update from the National Weather Service Prediction Center.  The coastal storm could also bring winter precipitation in the Mid-Mississippi Valley. On the West Coast, king tides combined with a bombardment of Pacific storm systems could cause flooding on low-lying California coastal roads and increase beach erosion through Thanksgiving. Weather hasn't been the only problem facing travelers. Delta Air Lines resolved an outage that caused delays nationwide Sunday, marking the third major disruption to U.S. air travel in nine days. AAA projects that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Tuesday, Nov. 24, and Monday, Nov. 30, including 72.9 million by car and 5.96 million on domestic flights. Tuesday and Wednesday: Atmospheric river in the West, storms in the Southeast AccuWeather's Pacific Coast hazards. AccuWeather In the Pacific Northwest and Northern California, a barrage of storm systems will bring rain and wintry precipitation to higher elevations on Tuesday, then move into Washington and Oregon on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the NWS. "Near the coast, there are Marginal Risks (level 1 of 4) of excessive rainfall today in Northern California, and on Wednesday and Thursday through portions of the coastal Pacific Northwest," the NWS said Tuesday. According to AccuWeather meteorologist Alyssa Glenny, "People heading to the coast for Thanksgiving should check high tide times and local road conditions. Storm-driven increases in water levels and wave action can make flooding worse when they overlap with high tide." Glenny also said that coastal flooding can happen even when it's not raining. In other words: sunshine doesn't necessarily mean the roads will be dry. In the San Francisco Bay Area, the storms coincide with potentially record-breaking king tides, the year's highest tides. The National Weather Service has a coastal flood warning in effect until 4 p.m. PT Thursday and calls Tuesday and Wednesday an "extreme" risk for flooding along the bay shoreline, and a high surf warning covers Wednesday on the Pacific coast. The agency said the storm will coincide with the king tides, potentially making flooding worse during Thanksgiving travel. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie wrote in a Tuesday X post , "On Wednesday, 11/25, we are expecting high tides and big swells around 11 am so stay away from Ocean Beach and the waterfront. Look out for each other, stay alert, and don't drive through floodwaters." In Marin County, Southern Marin Fire District has urged residents and businesses to "take action now" and prepare for possible road closures and travel disruptions. Further north, in Humboldt County, Sheriff William Honsal declared a local emergency and ordered residents of the King Salmon area on Humboldt Bay to leave by 7 a.m. Tuesday, after seawater flooded streets there during Monday's high tide, according to the sheriff's office . In the Southeast, heavy rain and thunderstorms could hit Atlanta and Charlotte on Wednesday, one of the busiest travel days of the year. AccuWeather said Wednesday could bring some of the most widespread weather-related travel disruptions before Thanksgiving, particularly in the Southeast, with airline delays expected to expand in Orlando and Miami from Tuesday to Wednesday and in Atlanta and Charlotte on Wednesday. The National Weather Service's Weather Prediction Center has warned of flooding rain along the coastal Carolinas on Wednesday. Delays at those hubs could ripple across the country. Thanksgiving Day: Possible major storm in the Northeast AccuWeather's holiday travel outlook. AccuWeather Forecasters are monitoring another storm that will form off the Southeast coast late Wednesday and move up the East Coast through Thanksgiving, bringing heavy rain and strong winds from the Mid-Atlantic to New England. "Significant coastal flooding and beach erosion are the primary concerns from Georgia to the Northeast, especially on Wednesday and Thursday; driven by strong onshore winds, high surf, and astronomical tides," according to the NWS. "The greatest impacts and flooding potential are expected along the Mid-Atlantic coast from the northern Outer Banks to New Jersey. Heavy rainfall is expected from the Southeast on Northward through southern New England." The National Weather Service in Boston called it a "potentially significant coastal storm" for Thanksgiving into Friday, with gusts along the coast possibly topping 50 mph. Very high tides could also bring coastal flooding, the agency said. The storm arrives as king tides continue on both coasts around Tuesday's full moon, which could worsen coastal flooding, the Weather Channel said. Interior parts of the Northeast and the Appalachians could see some snow or ice. AccuWeather said a brief period of wet snow or sleet is possible in northern New York and New England later Thursday. That could be a problem for the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York, which is set to start at 8:30 a.m. Thursday . The parade's giant balloons can't fly if sustained winds top 23 mph or gusts top 34 mph, Fox Weather reported . Rain is forecast to begin around midday, possibly before the parade ends, with conditions deteriorating significantly in the afternoon, AccuWeather reported. The weekend after Thanksgiving The National Weather Service expects the East Coast storm to weaken and move away, though windy conditions and some rain or snow showers could linger in parts of New England and the eastern Great Lakes into the weekend. Another storm could form in the East during the busy return weekend, while more Pacific storms could hit the West Coast. The Sunday after Thanksgiving is typically one of the busiest travel days of the year. Washington State Ferries has canceled several sailings because of high tides from Tuesday into the weekend, with about 300,000 people expected to use the ferry system over the holiday period. Forecasters advise travelers to check forecasts for both their departure and arrival cities, and to keep an eye on flight status before heading to the airport. articles.title: CIA and intel director’s office reportedly hit by hack affecting unclassified information
articles.summary: The main entrance of CIA headquarters in Langley, Virginia, on July 8, 2022. - Kevin Lamarque/Reuters/File The CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence suffered an apparent hack affecting unclassified information, four sources familiar with the matter told CNN. The intrusion hit a system the agencies draw on​ for open-source intelligence analysis, one of the sources said. The full extent of the breach was unclear, but officials emphasized that no classified information was affected. “There have been no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems,” an ODNI official told CNN. The CIA declined to comment. It is not immediately clear when the hack occurred, who was responsible for it, or if it has been resolved. The Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), which oversees 17 US intelligence agencies, including the CIA, has in recent years invested in open-source intelligence work, which is often unclassified. The apparent intrusion, which the New York Times first reported , is the latest in a string of cybersecurity incidents or tech outages that have rattled the US government and private sector. The incident does not appear to be related to an apparent hack of the FBI’s nationwide criminal information database, two of the sources said, which CNN first reported on Friday. The hacking incidents have coincided with a series of unrelated high-profile tech outages affecting banks, the National Security Agency and the FAA’s air traffic control system that have rattled Americans’ confidence in the technology that underpins their lives. All flights nationwide were grounded for hours earlier this month after a massive systems failure, leading to thousands of flights being delayed or canceled. The Federal Aviation Administration traced the problem to a single router in Arkansas. Separately, an outage affecting Microsoft products left people around the world unable to access staples of work life like Outlook email accounts and Teams meetings. But it’s the disruption at the NSA, the US’ signals intelligence spy agency, and intrusions at the FBI and CIA that have national security officials on alert. The highly classified network that the NSA uses for its internal communications went down for multiple days last week, CNN first reported . The apparent cause was a software update gone wrong and not a cyberattack, the nation’s spy chief Jay Clayton said. A critical Georgia facility that supports signals intelligence and cybersecurity operations focused on the Middle East, where the US is currently engaged in a war with Iran was also impacted, CNN reported . The NSA’s most sensitive and important intelligence-gathering systems were unaffected by the outage, and by Friday, the outage was resolved. The software vulnerabilities that the NSA was addressing are just a handful in a slew of new vulnerabilities that artificial intelligence has been able to locate. Cybersecurity experts say government agencies and companies alike are discovering a spate of new software bugs in their systems thanks to AI, prompting a rush to fix them and sometimes mistakes along the way. articles.title: Thanksgiving travelers are bracing for delays after a wave of airline tech outages
articles.summary: The timing couldn't have been worse. Just before the busiest travel week of the year, a wave of major aviation tech outages — including a Delta Air Lines system failure on Sunday, a United Airlines disruption last Monday and a nationwide FAA ground stop on Nov. 13 — looked sure to make leaving home for Thanksgiving more stressful than ever. Suddenly, "outage anxiety" was everywhere. "I think half the country is looking at its boarding pass with suspicion," Christopher Elliott, founder of a nonprofit that helps consumers resolve travel disputes, told the New York Times . According to a YouGov poll conducted right after the ground stop , nearly three-quarters of Americans (72%) said that if they were set to fly over the holiday, they would be concerned about experiencing "flight cancellations or significant delays as a result of further disruptions to U.S. air travel." And nearly a third (31%) said the ground stop could potentially alter their plans, making them less likely to travel by air for Thanksgiving. AAA projects nearly 6 million people will fly domestically over the seven-day Thanksgiving travel period. But now that the digital chaos seems to have subsided and Americans are starting to hit the road, how worried should you really be about additional meltdowns snarling your holiday travel plans? The simple answer: We don't know. An outage is, by definition, unexpected. The FAA said it was forced to ground thousands of flights after a router installed during a copper-to-fiber network upgrade flooded its telecommunications network with excessive data, overwhelming legacy equipment and destabilizing radar and communications feeds. Delta's outage was traced to a "database issue" in its automated weight-and-balance system. United's outage was similar. None were the result of a cyberattack, officials insisted. But none were foreseen, either. "This has never happened," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told CBS News , referring to the chain of events that triggered the ground stop. "And so that's why … we felt comfortable doing [the upgrade] in the middle of the day — because it's been done thousands of times. We've never had this situation." On Nov. 16, the Trump administration convened a "tiger team" — a small group of experts or specialists who work together on solving a specific problem that isn't easily addressed by normal operations — to prevent similar outages going forward. Composed of officials from the FAA, the Transportation Department, the Defense Department and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the team has "met every day this week to ensure continuity of service," according to the Daily Wire . A White House spokesperson said Americans preparing to travel for Thanksgiving have nothing to worry about, the outlet added. "President Trump and Secretary Duffy have brought together the best and the brightest across the government to ensure what happened [on Nov. 13] can never happen again," the spokesperson said. "Work continues, and Americans can rest assured their country's aviation is the best in the world." Why tech upgrades can cause outages But even if travelers survive the Thanksgiving rush without major incident, the experts suggest that future outages are simply inevitable . According to Microsoft President and Vice Chair Brad Smith — whose own company suffered a massive global outage earlier this month — AI is the common thread here, even if it didn't directly cause any of the recent travel disruptions. "What AI did earlier this year was basically make it much easier for people to find vulnerabilities in code, and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you're a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems," he told CBS News on Sunday . Smith went on to say that organizations are now rushing to patch vulnerabilities "at a pace we have never seen before" —a rush that itself creates instability, particularly within legacy systems. "Especially when you have older infrastructure, especially when you're trying to patch at such a pace, especially when you have to go so fast that you can't take as much time to test what you're changing in the code, you do increase the risk of something going wrong," he explained. The bottom line? Americans "have to be prepared" for more disruptions in "the coming months because this isn't the type of thing that just gets done in a couple of weeks," Smith said. "The whole information infrastructure of the world is in effect being upgraded right now." Even as the White House tries to reassure Thanksgiving travelers, administration officials have predicted that more outages are on the way. "The American people should understand that a great deal of our digital infrastructure is dated. It is old. It has been built out over three decades or more. We are in a period of technological step change, both in terms of what people refer to as [AI] models, applications, and the like, and in computing power," Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN on Sunday . "And in that technological step change, our systems are going to need to be upgraded," Clayton continued. "They're going to need to be upgraded for performance and for cybersecurity. And as part of that ongoing upgrade, we are going to have glitches, gaps, interruptions in service. That is going to happen." Asked if "the American people" should "just be prepared for more outages" because of those upgrades, Clayton effectively said yes. "They should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road," Clayton said. "Any time you refurbish your house, upgrade any of your systems, there are going to be things that you do not expect." How to prepare With that in mind, it's probably wise to plan for the worst if you're leaving home for the holiday — especially if you're flying. Print everything: boarding passes, visas and so on. Forgo checked bags, if possible. (Or at least track your luggage.) Keep your receipts. And know your rights : Transportation Department rules require airlines to issue a refund if your flight is canceled or significantly delayed for any reason (assuming you decline a replacement ticket or travel credit). After all, outages aren’t the only obstacle to consider this weekend. Major storms are also set to strike both coasts — including one that could last through Thanksgiving Day — and record-challenging king tides are threatening coastal flooding from California to Florida as a result of El Niño . articles.title: Al Gore returns to his roots with plan to buy his 113-year-old hometown newspaper
articles.summary: Al Gore is getting back into the newspaper business after starting his career as an Army journalist. But this time, he’s buying the paper. The former vice president is set to buy the Carthage Courier, his hometown paper in Tennessee, from the family of Hershel and Geraldine Lake, the Courier announced this week. The sale — which is expected to close in the coming weeks — would end the family’s 50-year run at the 113-year-old paper. “When my hometown paper came up for sale, I saw an opportunity to help preserve the Courier as an independent voice for Carthage and Smith County,” Gore said in a statement . The Courier, a weekly newspaper, said it will keep publishing through the transition and retain all of its staff. Before he ran for Congress in 1976, Gore spent six months as an Army journalist and worked as an investigative reporter for The Tennessean in Nashville. He went on to represent Tennessee in both chambers of Congress, before serving eight years as Bill Clinton’s vice president. Gore won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2007 alongside the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change and currently resides on his farm in Carthage. “I look forward to supporting the Carthage Courier team, many of whom have served this community for decades, as they continue to provide vital information and serve this community for generations to come,” Gore said. articles.title: CDC director responds to Democratic lawmakers' growing oversight of her tenure
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Three months into her tenure as head of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Dr. Erica Schwartz is being investigated by House Democrats, facing a call to resign, and drawing ire from both within and outside the agency. What's been happening at the nation's top public health agency has alarmed outside health professionals. It also has alienated staff, leaving morale as bad as ever, employees say. Schwartz, 54, took the helm of the CDC at a very challenging time: the worst U.S. measles epidemic in more than three decades, a large dengue fever outbreak in Florida and the fastest-growing overseas Ebola outbreak in history. She reports to U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who is a longtime critic of vaccines and federal public health policy and who played a role in decimating CDC staffing last year. “She has a tough job, at a tough time, and a tough boss,” said Noel Brewer, a University of North Carolina public health professor. In an interview with The Associated Press on Tuesday, Schwartz defended her work, saying she's trying to restore trust in the CDC — including by changing how measles-associated deaths are being reported. She said some of the criticisms are based on misperceptions and argued she is making progress on her goals. “I do understand why people have concerns," Schwartz told the AP from her home in Naples, Florida. “Have I made mistakes? Certainly. But I'm here to work on the behalf of the American people.” Some experts say she has made the situation worse. And critics are seizing on the Pan American Health Organization’s declaration last week that measles is continuously spreading here, marking the re-establishment of a public health threat that was eliminated in the last century. “I have no confidence that she will do what it takes to course-correct at the CDC, and she should resign immediately,” said U.S. Sen. Michael Bennet, a Colorado Democrat. Schwartz has an impressive resume When President Donald Trump nominated Schwartz to be the next CDC director in April, he called her “a STAR!” on social media. She holds both medical and law degrees. She was chief medical officer for the U.S. Coast Guard, where she oversaw 41 clinics and 150 sick bays. She served as deputy surgeon general in the U.S. Public Health Service, helping to lead uniformed medical and health professionals posted at the CDC and government health agencies. Many public health leaders were cautiously optimistic, noting the CDC badly needed steady leadership after enduring more than a year of turmoil and months of being led by interim directors. Schwartz was the third Trump nominee for CDC director in less than 18 months. The first was a former Florida congressman whose nomination was pulled an hour before a Senate confirmation hearing. The second was Susan Monarez, who won Senate approval but then was ousted less than a month into the job when Trump administration officials said she was not aligned with the president’s agenda. Under Kennedy, the agency has seen around 30% of its staff leave, mostly through layoffs, resignations and retirements. At her nomination hearing , Schwartz pledged “radical transparency” to rebuild public trust in the agency, which she noted declined during the COVID-19 pandemic and which has eroded further under Kennedy. “I will always stand on science and speak the truth, even in difficult moments,” she testified. Meanwhile, public misperceptions about vaccines have persisted. A recent Annenberg Public Policy Center survey found that about 1 in 6 Americans said they believed that “vaccines given to children for diseases like measles, mumps and rubella cause autism” — even though dozens of studies have determined there’s no causal link. Roughly another 1 in 5 said they didn’t know whether it was true. Schwartz hasn’t held a news conference Schwartz started at the Atlanta-based agency in mid-August. A week later, she held her first “all hands” staff meeting , during which she promised to advocate for the agency and said she wouldn’t hesitate to disagree with Kennedy — but only privately. Some say that’s when their optimism for Schwartz began to fade. “I don’t have a clear sense of what is important to her, what are her red lines,” one CDC health scientist told the AP. “If we’re talking about radical transparency,” it is appropriate to know on what issues and what messaging she will not compromise, the scientist added. The employee spoke on condition of anonymity for fear of retribution. Asked about that assessment, Schwartz said: “I would never do anything unethical or illegal. ... That is a red line.” Despite that transparency pledge, CDC and HHS officials for months would not release Schwartz’s salary — even though it is public information. Schwartz is paid about $375,000 a year, CDC officials finally told the AP this week, above the typical range for previous CDC directors. So far she also has been less visible than some predecessors. She has not held any news conferences, and has not used her bully pulpit to try to persuade more Americans to get vaccinations — including for measles, the flu and COVID-19. Schwartz told the AP that, concerning measles, she doesn't believe a federal health official on TV will sway most of the unvaccinated. But with the nation experiencing its worst measles epidemic in decades, many public health and medical leaders say Schwartz should be strongly urging Americans to get vaccinated. “I hope to see her display independence from the vaccine rhetoric and challenges that have been part of this administration,” said Dr. Wendy Armstrong, president of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. “I don’t think we have seen that yet.” Kennedy continues to back Schwartz. The Health and Human Services Department issued a statement in response to Associated Press queries, quoting Kennedy as saying she had his full support. “Dr. Schwartz brings the judgment to make hard decisions and the courage to see them through. She is reforming CDC and sharpening its focus on its core mission: protecting Americans from disease,” the statement said. Congressional Democrats are launching investigations Some Democratic legislators accuse Schwartz and Kennedy of downplaying measles. Kennedy has challenged health officials’ accounts of measles deaths. And the CDC has stopped quickly relaying state reports of measles deaths. It adopted a new policy requiring the review of death certificates, which has resulted in CDC counting only about half the measles-associated deaths that states are reporting. Schwartz said that was her decision, and stemmed from her desire to have a uniform definition of what counts as a measles death. Democrats on the House Energy & Commerce Committee have questioned why CDC changed the policy. “As the crisis worsens, we are concerned that you continue to direct an effort at CDC to downplay the outbreak and artificially reduce the number of deaths that CDC reports,” according to a statement from Reps. Frank Pallone Jr. of New Jersey, Diana DeGette of Colorado and Yvette Clarke of New York. “We are expanding our investigation to examine the threats your actions pose to Americans’ health and whether changes to your statutory authority are required,” they added. The statement followed a briefing at which Schwartz was supposed to answer congressional staffers' questions about the measles data. The committee leaders described Schwartz as unresponsive and, at times, misleading. Schwartz argued that she was “fully transparent. And I am really concerned that they think there is more to the story. There isn't.” CDC employees see little sign of progress The AP interviewed eight current CDC workers about Schwartz's tenure. They all spoke on condition of anonymity, saying they feared retribution for speaking frankly about what’s going on within the agency. Some said they never had high expectations. Others said they initially were hopeful but lost confidence, some of them blaming her handling of the measles death count. One said it’s still too early to judge her. Several said they had hoped for more improvements and stability. Announcements about leadership appointees coming, going and changing titles have continued in a blur, the employees told the AP. Some mentioned Caroline DeBerry, a former vice president at a conservative think tank and author of independently published novels including one titled “Esther: The Woman Who Didn’t Know Her Place.” DeBerry got a job as acting director of communications, starting in August. Employees said she gained notoriety within the agency when all CDC website updates ground to a halt while awaiting her approval. Asked about it, Schwartz said: “There was a bit of clunkiness that happened one day.” She also said DeBerry is on “terminal leave” and her last day will be in December, but did not immediately offer additional detail. None of the agency veterans interviewed by the AP said they have spoken with Schwartz. But some said they had seen her around the CDC campus accompanied by a group of security guards. Security has been a sensitive topic at CDC, especially since an August 2025 shooting outside the entrance of CDC’s main campus. A Georgia man who had blamed the COVID-19 vaccine for making him depressed and suicidal opened fire, killing a police officer and spraying bullets into 150 windows . (The slain officer, David Rose, is widely held up as a hero by CDC employees, and some expressed irritation that Schwartz referred to him as “Officer Stone” during a recent health summit appearance.) Dr. Tom Frieden, who served as CDC director in the Obama administration, said he occasionally had an escort outside the CDC campus after he received death threats. But Schwartz moves with a large security team inside CDC, and agency staffers said they don’t recall seeing that before. “It feels like they’re afraid of us,” one health scientist said. Schwartz acknowledged that early in her time at CDC, she walked the halls accompanied by about a half dozen guards at the recommendation of security leadership. The security details have been reduced to one plainclothes guard, she said. Confusion over the publication of scientific reports A directive about research publications shows just how far apart CDC staff feel from the political leadership. Two CDC scientists told the AP that they were directed in a recent meeting to stop submitting their research to journals run by organizations that have sued Kennedy. The prohibition would cover Pediatrics, one of the most-cited journals for doctors who specialize in children’s medical care, and Clinical Infectious Diseases, a highly regarded publication for doctors focused on germs. The scientists said the directive was clearly stated but not written down in a memo or email. HHS and CDC officials are adamant that neither Kennedy nor any other HHS or CDC official ever issued such a directive. At the health summit, Schwartz acknowledged that CDC employees have lost trust in the political appointees who have been put in charge of the agency, “and I’m trying to earn that trust every day.” She talked about work going on to stabilize the agency’s leadership and develop a “strategic hiring plan” for 2027. CDC employees look around and see burned-out colleagues. “I think everyone is just exhausted,” one health scientist said. “There’s just a sense that we can’t go on like this anymore.” ___ The Associated Press’ health and science coverage receives financial support from the AP Fund for Journalism and private foundations. articles.title: One every 4 minutes: 720,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war, new data suggests
articles.summary: A monument to the dead overlooks a massive burial site of Russian soldiers in the rural Volga region of Kostroma, Russia, on October 20, 2025. - Andrey Borodulin/AFP/Getty Images Almost three-quarters of a million Russian soldiers have been killed since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, equating to roughly one death every four minutes, analysis based on leaked official data has revealed. Russian opposition outlets Mediazona and Meduza reported on Monday that by the end of September, 490,000 Russian troops had been confirmed dead by Russia’s statistical bureau, Rosstat. But accounting for time lags in reporting and including troops who have been reported as missing in action – and are most likely dead – Russian fatalities jump to more than 720,000 since the start of the war, according to the two outlets. That is a staggering number that surpasses Russia’s death toll from the Soviet war in Afghanistan in the 1980s and both Chechen wars in the 1990s and early 2000s – and which the Kremlin has long tried to keep secret. Rosstat stopped publishing demographic data in 2025 to disguise the rising death toll from the war. Mediazona and Meduza, as well as other outlets, obtained the official data after two pro-Ukrainian hacker groups, Cyber ​​Partisans of Belarus and Silent Crow, managed to breach Rosstat’s servers earlier this month. CNN cannot independently verify the figures, but the leaked data on confirmed deaths alone corroborates earlier estimates by analysts and Western intelligence – which now appear to fall far short of the likely real death toll. Mediazona and Meduza have long been keeping a tally of Russian losses, based mostly on inheritance documents, death notices and other publicly available documents. Ukrainian servicemen fire a self-propelled howitzer towards Russian positions in eastern Ukraine on December 28, 2022. - Sameer Al-Doumy/AFP/Getty Images But the leaked Rosstat data allowed the media outlets to go a step further, using the same methods and calculations normally employed by actuaries estimating risks and insurance premiums. By analyzing discrepancies between reported death dates and death registration dates, and by comparing these to search notices published by relatives, the reporters were able to extrapolate the number of deaths that have occurred but have not yet been reported to be somewhere around 230,000. Mediazona has kept a tally of troops identified as missing by their relatives from 2023. That database contains 160,000 individuals and almost all of them are likely dead. Mediazona said that based on its reporting, the rate of survival among those reported missing only around 10%. unknown content item - The data shared by Silent Crow showed that the war was the fourth most common cause of death in Russia since the start of the full-scale invasion, after heart diseases; Covid; and stroke and other vascular conditions. It also confirms what has long been suspected – that the losses are not spread evenly across Russia, with poorer areas and ethnic minorities suffering significantly higher casualty rates. In addition, an analysis by the NEST Centre, a think tank that also obtained the data, revealed the scale of Russia’s recruitment of foreign fighters. It identified 6,947 records of foreign nationals killed in Ukraine – the majority of them from the central Asian countries of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Turkmenistan. Like Russia, Ukraine doesn’t release official casualty data, although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has publicly acknowledged the scale of losses in combat. The most recent research by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimated in July that the country has endured between 525,000 and 625,000 casualties, including 125,000 and 150,000 fatalities. Alexander Baunov, a senior fellow at the Carnegie Russia Eurasia Center, said that the combined death toll suffered by Russia and Ukraine could exceed 1 million. Ukraine expands evacuation orders As the newly projected death toll underscores the human cost of Moscow’s war, fears are growing in Ukraine over a deteriorating security situation in the country’s eastern Donetsk region – an area mostly under Russian control – amid daily guided bomb and drone attacks . All families with children still in Donetsk were on Tuesday ordered to evacuate. Children and families in many communities in most of Ukrainian-controlled Donetsk - including the major cities of Kramatorsk and Sloviansk - were already under the evacuation order, but now the measure has been expanded to settlements further west. An estimated 64,500 civilians remain in the region as of November 2026, according to the Donetsk regional military administration. “This is an extremely difficult but necessary decision. The Russians are shelling our cities and villages every day and bombarding the region with aerial bombs,” said the head of Donetsk’s regional military administration, Vadym Filashkin. For months, Moscow’s forces have been inching towards Kramatorsk , one of Ukraine’s last strongholds in the north of Donetsk region. Tuesday’s mandatory evacuation order is a sign of Kyiv’s concern that an expansion of Russian attacks could further harm civilians and isolate communities, for example by blowing up bridges and supply routes. CNN’s Clare Sebastian, Nathan Hodge, Kosta Gak and Lauren Kent contributed reporting. articles.title: 索罗斯的“帝国循环”：为什么美国绝不愿让AI泡沫轻易破裂？
articles.summary: 一夜之间，华尔街重新相信了AI的未来。11月23日，黄仁勋重返英伟达首席执行官职位，英伟达股价上涨约31.5%，纳斯达克综合指数上涨约6.5%，标普500上涨约4.7%。此前，市场还在讨论AI资本开支是否已经失控、数据中心债务能否偿还，以及这场技术革命是否正在重演互联网泡沫。一次人事变化，就让市场迅速完成了数万亿美元级别的重新定价。 黄仁勋回归确实消除了一项重要的经营与治理不确定性，却没有在一夜之间改变数据中心的折旧、模型公司的收入或算力项目的偿债能力。股价先于这些经营变量发生变化，恰好揭示了金融市场一种古老而强大的机制：人们对未来的判断，会反过来改变今天的融资条件和经济行为。四十多年前，乔治·索罗斯曾用“帝国循环”描述美国身上的类似现象。今天重新翻开这套理论，或许比急于判断美股是否见顶更有意义。 01 美国的财富循环，是怎样转起来的？ 1. 美国越借钱，为什么世界反而愿意送钱？ 1984年，里根政府的财政赤字、强势美元和美国经济复苏同时出现。按通常的直觉，一个财政支出持续大于收入、贸易逆差日益扩大的国家，应当受到资金和汇率的约束。索罗斯看到的却是一套自我强化的循环：财政扩张刺激需求，经济复苏和较高的美元资产回报吸引海外资金，资本流入支撑美元；强美元又让进口商品更便宜，在一定程度上抑制通胀，使美国能够继续消费、融资和扩张。 索罗斯将其称为里根的“帝国循环”。它的妙处在于，财政赤字、贸易赤字与美元强势原本可能彼此冲突，却在一段时期相互支撑。美国向外部购买商品，世界又愿意持有美元资产，借款者因融资能力改善而继续扩张，债权人因美国增长强劲而更愿意提供资金。这套机制的起点并非美国可以无代价举债，而是全球资本愿意不断认可美国的经济表现和金融资产。 2. 四十年里，财富引擎换了动力： 今天的美国与1984年早已不同。高利率和财政刺激仍然重要，但吸引全球资本的理由更加丰富。美元是国际贸易、金融结算和储备资产的重要载体；美国国债市场拥有罕见的深度和流动性；大型科技企业则凭借技术、品牌、规模经济和全球客户，创造了长期可观的利润与自由现金流。全球投资者进入美国，既是购买一种货币体系，也是购买一组具有竞争力的企业和金融资产。 ……

articles.summary: 近期一系列高调网络安全事件令市场警觉，也让OpenAI看到了新的商业机会。 OpenAI总裁Greg Brockman近日明确表态，网络安全将成为该公司比编程更大的业务板块。首席财务官Sarah Friar则称，目前市场对网络安全总可寻址市场逾3000亿美元的估算，远远低估了这一领域的真实潜力。 上述表态出现在OpenAI为备战潜在IPO、积极寻求新收入来源的关键节点。然而，OpenAI如何将这一愿景落地，目前仍缺乏清晰路径，且面临来自Anthropic、谷歌等竞争对手的正面挑战。 网络安全事件频发，OpenAI嗅到商机 据The Information最新报道，近期多起高知名度网络安全事件相继冲击银行、政府机构及关键基础设施，其中包括美国联邦调查局（FBI）全国犯罪数据库遭黑客攻击一事——白宫已于上周末证实这一事件。 尽管目前尚不清楚AI技术是否在上述攻击中扮演了角色，但这些事件已加剧外界对AI技术助长网络犯罪的担忧。对OpenAI而言，这股围绕网络安全的恐慌情绪，同时也意味着一个潜在的重大商业机会。 这也引出一个颇为微妙的问题：如果OpenAI等AI公司的模型在客观上加剧了网络攻击，客户是否会愿意同时接受OpenAI既"卖 毒药"又"卖解药"？ Brockman描绘三步走路线图 当被问及OpenAI如何从网络安全中盈利时，Greg Brockman向The Information描述了三个步骤：构建优质的网络安全专用模型，将其交付给经过验证的可信客户（他强调，功能强大的安全产品不能随意出售），再教会这些客户如何使用。 "毫无疑问，网络安全将成为OpenAI比编程更大的业务。"Brockman说。 Sarah Friar则补充道，尽管部分估算将网络安全当前总可寻址市场定在逾3000亿美元，但这一数字"远远低估了"该领域的潜力。 Daybreak项目：2000家机构，付费规模待考 OpenAI目前主要通过2025年5月推出的Daybreak项目分发安全产品。该项目要求客户在使用前完成身份验证。 OpenAI于2025年9月披露，约有2000家机构和企业正在使用Daybreak，但付费客户的具体数量尚未公开。产品按token计费。同月，OpenAI还宣布承诺投入10亿美元，为州及地方政府、社区银行、非营利组织等"资源受限"机构补贴使用成本。 Sarah Friar表示，OpenAI已在现有企业客户中取得一定进展——Expedia和Amgen均在第三季度首次购买了OpenAI的网络安全产品。其他主要客户还包括摩根大通和Visa。值得注意的是，摩根大通、Visa和Expedia近期均曾遭遇网络攻击。 OpenAI拒绝披露网络安全业务的具体营收数据。 竞争激烈，IBM“两手都要抓” OpenAI在网络安全赛道并不孤单。Anthropic同样在持续推出安全能力更强的模型，并瞄准与OpenAI高度重叠的客户群体。谷歌也在积极宣传其近期发布的Gemini 4系列模型在网络安全方面的能力。 IBM全球网络安全业务总经理Mark Hughes向The Information表示，IBM目前同时使用OpenAI和Anthropic的安全模型，两家公司各有所长。他举例称，OpenAI的某款模型在高级安全测试（包括红队测试）方面表现突出，而Anthropic的模型则在编写代码时修复漏洞方面更具优势。 "我们必须做到的，是真正取各家之所长。"Hughes说。这一态度或许也代表了其他大型客户的普遍立场。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 小米：拐点已现？
articles.summary: 尽管小米三季度业绩承压，但高盛、花旗与巴克莱均维持买入或增持评级，认为小米收入同比降幅持续收窄，盈利修正正在触底，2027年的复苏轨道日益清晰。 追风交易台消息，11月25日，高盛分析师Timothy Zhao团队研报中指出，小米2026年三季度业绩基本符合预期，调整后净利润同比下滑57%至49亿元，较高盛预期高出1%。 与此同时， 高盛认为盈利修正正在接近底部，叠加存储成本、物联网增长、海外扩张及AI等核心叙事出现改善信号，核心运营费用自三季度起实现同比削减，这一趋势有望延续数个季度，维持买入评级。 花旗 分析师Kyna Wong团队同日发布报告，同样维持买入评级，看好物联网与手机业务2027年双复苏。 巴克莱 分析师Jiong Shao团队则于11月24日维持增持评级，明确表态小米是2027年"最佳布局标的之一"。 三家机构的共识在于：四季度有望成为收入同比回正的第一个季度，标志着公司重回增长轨道。 手机业务：以价换量，毛利率超预期 三季度，小米智能手机出货量同比下滑29%至3070万部，但均价同比大幅提升40%至人民币1486元，推动手机收入同比降幅收窄至仅-0.8%，毛利率达到9.2%，环比提升0.6个百分点，高于多数机构预期。 据高盛研报，小米手机毛利率的韧性体现了公司在出货量下滑背景下，平衡均价提升与物料成本上涨之间的执行能力。 管理层在业绩会上表示，NAND价格已趋于稳定甚至略有上涨，DRAM成本则将持续上行至2028年上半年之前，原因是供给增长有限且需求无放缓迹象。 管理层表示将通过产品创新和组合优化来对冲成本压力，并对2027年维持稳健毛利率水平保持信心。 花旗报告指出 ，公司全年智能手机出货量指引维持在1.2亿部，这意味着四季度出货量约为2450万部，同比下降约35%。 巴克莱则预计 ，更高的手机售价将对2027年出货增长形成拖累，但均价的持续提升将支撑整体收入增长。 物联网：同比降幅大幅收窄，拐点将至 物联网（IoT）业务是本季度另一个积极信号。 三季度IoT收入同比仅下滑1.4%，较一、二季度的-24%和-19%大幅收窄。 高盛研报指出，这一改善主要源于电视和家电收入同比转正，以及中国区IoT收入降幅收窄至个位数。 高盛预测，IoT收入将于四季度实现同比正增长约6%，2027年进一步加速至13%。 巴克莱则更为乐观，预计IoT业务四季度同比增速或达双位数。 管理层在业绩会上披露，海外市场约贡献IoT收入的30%，截至三季度末小米在海外拥有逾750家米家新零售门店，管理层表示将加速海外品类与渠道扩张。 花旗预计，全年IoT收入同比下滑约10%，但2027年将恢复13%的同比增长，并将IoT毛利率预测小幅上调至22.1%。 运营费用：七个季度以来首次同比下降 三季度，小米核心运营费用同比减少约10亿元，主要来自管理费用压降及研发效率提升，这也是自2023年四季度以来的首次核心运营费用同比下降。 高盛对此给予较高评价 ，援引小米此前2022年二季度至2023年四季度连续七个季度实现运营费用同比下降的历史记录， 认为此番运营费用削减的可持续性有据可查。 高盛预测2026/2027年小米核心运营费用同比增速分别为持平和+2%，为2027年盈利能力改善提供更好的运营杠杆。 从整体盈利来看，三季度调整后净利润为49亿元，同比下滑57%，但高于花旗和彭博一致预期约3%。核心业务（剔除智能电动车）调整后净利润为83亿元，利润率7.7%，高于巴克莱预期16个基点。 智能电动车：交付放量，毛利率平稳 智能电动车业务在三季度延续稳健表现。 小米三季度共交付约10.1万辆，其中澎程系列自9月13日开启交付起贡献逾1万辆，并在首30天内锁定超过7万份订单。三季度电动车及其他新业务板块毛利率维持在19.2%，与二季度持平。 管理层在业绩会上对澎程的市场定位表示乐观，称其与SU7/YU7之间为增量而非蚕食关系，超过50%的买家年龄在35岁以上，88%为家庭用户，且逾半数为首次购车或替换燃油车。 受澎程放量带动，10月交付量突破5万辆，管理层预计11月及12月均可维持在5万辆以上，全年交付量指引约45万辆，即四季度约16至17万辆。 高盛预测全年电动车交付量约44.6万辆，2027/2028年分别升至57万辆和73.1万辆。 在海外扩张方面，管理层透露小米计划于2027年下半年进入欧洲市场，初期以整车出口方式销售，并已在德国签署合作协议、完成多国路试，同时已启动本地生产的可行性评估。 AI与机器人：投入加码，商业化路径渐晰 三季度研发费用达92亿元，同比增长2%，其中AI相关研发占比超过30%。 高盛分析师认为，三季度IFRS口径下电动车及其他新业务经营亏损达34亿元，大于预期，主要源于更高的算力投入。 据高盛研报，小米于9月底发布了MiMo-V2.6系列，并同步推进基于HySparse2新架构的MiMo-V3训练，该架构在降低prefill延迟、缩小KV缓存的同时，改善了Agent推理场景下的长文本检索能力。 在机器人领域，小米已实现CyberOne人形机器人在工厂执行8小时分拣任务，并基于自研Xiaomi-Robotics-1具身基础模型开展青年公寓机器人试运营。管理层表示，具身AI机器人市场的商业潜力甚至可能超过汽车行业。 巴克莱研报亦指出，小米在自研芯片（XRING O3、O100、D100）、HyperOS操作系统及MiMo大模型方面的布局，使其在"人x车x家"生态中构建AI能力具有显著的协同优势。 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 以上精彩内容来自 追风交易台 。 更详细的解读，包括实时解读、一线研究等内容，请加入【 追风交易台▪年度会员 】 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 阴霾笼罩年底市场！摩根大通：伊朗军事升级、美联储紧缩、政府关门、关税上调、芯片管制一起来了！
articles.summary: 距离2026年结束还有五周，市场却要同时面对一张密密麻麻的风险清单。 据追风交易台消息，11月19日，摩根大通全球研究主席Joyce Chang率团队在华盛顿与政策制定者、官方债权人及独立智库人士举行了一整天的闭门会议。该行于11月24日发布报告，将会议核心内容整理为"中期选举后需监测的十大风险"。 报告开篇基调沉重。分析师写道，"从华盛顿回来后，我们对中期选举后的风险更加谨慎"，而那一周几乎每一类资产都在下跌，美债和美元是仅有的例外。 报告援引当天最令人印象深刻的一句警告： "AI融资的解体，加上美联储的进一步紧缩，可能造就'一个非常难看的圣诞节'——股市大幅下跌，直到美联储被迫转向，就像2018年末那样。" 伊朗：12月可能是最危险的窗口 与会者为伊朗局势勾勒出三条路径：谈判达成和解（概率20%-25%）、维持现状（30%-40%）、美国重启军事行动（30%-40%）。 谈判前景之所以渺茫，在于双方诉求差距悬殊——美国坚持"经济绞杀"策略，伊朗则要求立即解除封锁、撤销制裁、美军撤出地区。报告描述伊朗领导层"越来越被专注于政权存续的伊斯兰革命卫队强硬派所主导"。 时间节点上，与会者特别点出了 12月9日至11日 。理由直白：这几天月相处于当月最暗的夜晚，"历史上有利于进攻方"。若特朗普总统授权行动，与会者认为更可能是针对伊朗剩余核设施的5至6天短暂密集空袭，而非涉及地面部队的持久战——"美军伤亡的可能性让地面部队的部署在政治上极不吸引人"。 油价方面，该行大宗商品策略师Natasha Kaneva的团队泼了一盆冷水。他们预测2027年和2028年全球石油将分别出现160万桶/日和140万桶/日的供应过剩，布伦特原油年底2027将跌至 66美元/桶 。报告指出，"当前油价已将攻击概率计入其中，考虑到9月油市已转为供应过剩、10月过剩进一步扩大，现货价格高出合理水平5至7美元"。 短期军事升级可能带来油价的暂时性冲高，但基本面的供应过剩压力将随后主导走势。 美联储：加息加到“出错”的风险 美联储的路径争议是本次华盛顿会议的另一焦点。 主张美联储落后于曲线的一方认为，由于美国财政缺乏约束，中性利率可能比疫情前高出100至150个基点，政策传导也因企业和家庭可绕过政策利率获得其他融资而减弱。一位与会者预期美联储将再加息三次，每次25个基点，分别在12月、1月和3月至4月。摩根大通美国经济团队的基准预测与此一致：三次加息后，联邦基金利率目标区间升至 4.50%-4.75% ，随后暂停至年底。 但另一派的担忧同样尖锐。伊朗冲突将油价从约60美元/桶推升至100美元/桶以上，触发了美联储措辞的明显转变，但"冲击主要集中在整体通胀，核心通胀相对稳定"。 这派人士指出，若油价回落至60美元/桶，将通过能源价格和基数效应大幅压低整体通胀；若跌至40至50美元/桶，则可能通过运输和其他能源敏感成本带动更广泛的通缩，"核心通胀有可能在其他分项保持稳定的情况下接近2%"。 "风险在于，美联储根据滞后数据持续加息，而供给冲击恰恰在此时逆转。" 报告还提到，首次购房者进入市场的年龄已推迟至40多岁，7.5%左右的抵押贷款利率和结构性供应不足是主要障碍。在能源冲击已是暂时性的背景下，用加息来打压通胀，代价由住房市场承担，这一逻辑受到质疑。 AI融资：7万亿美元的大厦，地基有多稳？ 摩根大通信贷策略团队预测， 2027年至2031年间AI资本开支总额将达7万亿美元 ，仅2027年就约1.4万亿美元，几乎是2026年的两倍。 问题是，钱从哪里来。报告指出，"每年1.4万亿美元的融资规模，已经触及债务市场所能承受的上限"，AI投资尚未实现自我造血，2027年和2028年的融资组合中将有更大比例来自股权资本。目前信贷支持安排存量约 3720亿美元 。 更令人警惕的是循环融资结构。报告援引IMF的研究：IMF审查了2023年以来的14笔相关交易，发现约3000亿美元的股权投资和6500亿美元的债务，换取了1.4万亿美元的未来收入承诺。"IMF警告，杠杆和这些融资关联可能在AI投资或盈利不及预期时放大市场调整。" 供应商融资、无追索权贷款和租赁安排引发了另一层担忧——这些安排让企业以高价购入资产，同时将大部分下行风险转移给贷款方，"形成融资支撑高交易价格、高价格反过来验证更高估值的自我强化循环"。 万七系（Mag-7）公司在2026年第三季度财报期的盈利增速，自2022年以来首次低于标普500其余成分股。 关税：年底前有效税率可能升至15%-20% 关税不是在被逆转，而是在被重建。 该行经济学家Jahangir Aziz和Abiel Reinhart在11月13日的报告中指出，预计一系列301条款和232条款关税即将宣布，以将平均有效关税税率恢复至IEEPA被法院推翻前的2月水平。 具体而言，当局正在对16个经济体的"结构性产能过剩"展开301条款调查，结果即将公布；与此同时，232条款调查范围也在扩大，涵盖钢铁、铝、铜等产品， 有效关税税率可能从当前7%-8%升至15%-20% 。 加拿大方面可能获得一定豁免，民主党也可能寻求废除对加拿大的338条款关税作为早期政治胜利，但整体方向是关税上行，而非逆转。 芯片管制：在新国会就职前抢先出手 英伟达争议在两党之间形成了加强出口管制的政治动力，白宫有动力在1月3日新国会就职前率先划定规则。 管制范围正在从传统芯片出口扩展至 远程算力访问、芯片制造设备和AI基础设施投资 。报告提到四项相关法案可能被纳入《国防授权法案》（NDAA），包括覆盖美国数据中心远程访问的《远程访问安全法》（RASA）、针对AI技术管控的《AI监察》法案、针对先进半导体制造设备的MATCH法案，以及打击芯片走私的相关立法。 政府关门：市场低估了风险 12月11日是政府资金截止日期，也是国会与白宫的第一个正面冲突点。 新的民主党多数将以此作为筹码，核心争议在于《国防授权法案》（NDAA）。民主党面临两难：既要为五角大楼拨款，又不想被视为授权伊朗战争继续进行。 报告指出，国会预算办公室（CBO）估计截至2026年8月1日，伊朗冲突已令国防部花费约 380亿美元 ，此后每月还将产生30亿美元或更多支出；五角大楼自己的估计截至11月13日为 483亿美元 。若将对经济和消费者的更广泛影响纳入，宾夕法尼亚大学沃顿预算模型的独立估算高达 2100亿美元 。 政府关门风险因伊朗战争拨款争议而上升，报告明确指出，"关门风险对市场的冲击可能超出市场当前的预期"。 财政：两党都不愿动刀 美国财政赤字2026年预计占GDP的 6.2% ，摩根大通经济学家预测2027年为6.1%、2028年升至6.4%。 与会者的一致结论令人沮丧：两党都没有政治意愿去削减支出以稳定赤字。共和党难以削减社保、医保和医疗补助；民主党的优先事项是恢复ACA补贴、逆转医疗补助和SNAP削减，这只会增加开支。 财政部长贝森特寄望于"3-3-3"策略——额外增加300万桶/日能源产量、实现3%经济增长、将财政赤字压缩至GDP的3%——但报告直言，"3%赤字目标在本届总统任期结束前远不可能实现"。 CBO测算，若利率在其2026年2月基准之上持续高出50个基点，2026年至2036年间将累计增加约 1.6万亿美元 净利息支出、1.9万亿美元总赤字；若高出150个基点，则分别增加约 4.9万亿美元 和 6万亿美元 。 与会者的共识是：可能需要一次重大的市场或经济冲击，才能迫使政策制定者采取行动。 市场含义：25%的跌幅能承受吗？ 摩根大通报告最后用了相当篇幅讨论市场的承受能力。 与会者普遍认为，若AI修正引发市场抛售，其性质更接近2001年而非2008年——不会触发系统性危机，因为芯片等计算资产经济寿命约五年，估值扭曲的持续时间有限，银行资本充足，家庭和企业资产负债表也比全球金融危机前健康。 但也有与会者提出更悲观的情景：美国股市市值已达GDP的 250% （截至2026年6月），若AI融资解体、科技出口管制收紧与美联储持续加息三者叠加，可能产生类似2018年末的更显著调整。 哈佛经济学家Jason Furman的测算显示，美股下跌25%可能使消费在随后一年减少约0.8%，拖累GDP增速约0.6个百分点；若考虑财富效应对消费的完整影响，冲击可能高达3.4个百分点。他的假设情景还显示，若英伟达、微软、谷歌、亚马逊、Meta、博通和甲骨文这七大AI股下跌50%，可能带动大盘下跌约 11% 。 IMF的模型则显示，AI冲击可能触发美股下跌20%、其他市场下跌15%，美国GDP在2028年减少0.8%，全球GDP减少0.4%。 在资产配置上，摩根大通倾向于高质量固定收益和美元，而非黄金。报告指出，在约2.7%的核心PCE通胀预测背景下，约6%的稳定收益率具有吸引力，目前约26%的证券收益率超过6%。美元方面，摩根大通外汇策略团队预测欧元兑美元将跌至 1.05 。 articles.title: 数据中心需求推动，美国钢铁价格飙至四年高位
articles.summary: 人工智能基础设施建设热潮正在重塑美国钢铁市场格局。数据中心建设需求超出预期，令美国国内钢铁供应趋于紧张，价格攀升至四年高位，同时也在悄然瓦解特朗普政府关税政策的保护效果。 美国热轧卷板价格近期报价已突破每短吨1300美元，较一年前不足900美元的水平大幅跃升。 美国最大钢铁生产商Nucor本周将热轧卷板挂牌价上调至每短吨1330美元，延续了自夏季以来连续数周上涨的态势。与此同时，据Jefferies分析师Albert Realini在近期报告中指出，部分进口钢铁在计入关税及运输成本后，仍比美国国内供应便宜近400美元每吨。（短吨为美国常用重量单位，1短吨等于 2000磅 ，约合 907.185千克 ） 据彭博11月25日报道，在价格高企的驱动下，亚洲进口钢铁正重新涌入美国市场。尽管特朗普政府对外国钢铁征收50%的关税，韩国、越南等东亚供应商的出货量近月来仍显著攀升，令这一轮关税保护的实际效力受到考验。花旗集团分析师Alexander Hacking在报告中写道， 美国市场“无疑正处于一场显著挤压之中，由终端客户库存偏低、数据中心需求以及季节性补库共同驱动” ，并指出“这一挤压何时缓解，目前尚难判断”。 数据中心建设热潮推高钢铁需求 据报道，人工智能的快速扩张及其所需的电力基础设施，已将美国钢铁需求推至超出预期的水平。数据中心项目从地基浇筑到服务器机架、通风管道，各环节均大量消耗钢铁，项目订单迅速排满，国内钢厂应接不暇。 富国银行分析师Timna Tanners将当前局面描述为“对钢材的疯狂争夺”。她表示，“美国钢厂给买家的钢铁供应不足，他们正在削减延伸至2027年的供货协议。” 对于小型制造商而言，供应紧张的影响尤为直接。专门生产定制钢丝及钣金产品的Marlin Steel首席执行官Drew Greenblatt表示，他只从美国本土生产商采购，而目前向钢厂下单后的交货周期已从一年前的一至三天延长至八至十二周。为此，他选择超量备货以维持对客户的持续供货。 “我们不得不向客户重新解释定价，这非常尴尬。所以我现在尽量多买，这样才能保持对他们的发货量。我们买的远比实际需要的多。” 亚洲进口钢铁重返美国市场 尽管关税壁垒高企，东亚钢铁出口商已找到重新进入美国市场的空间。据美国钢铁协会数据，截至10月，韩国平轧钢进口量较2025年同期激增68%。越南10月的钢铁进口申请量较9月最终进口量翻逾一倍，达到21.3万净吨，使其成为当月美国第四大外国钢铁供应商。 韩国钢铁行业由POSCO Holdings和Hyundai Steel Co.等巨头主导，两家公司产能充裕，且在国内需求持续低迷的背景下积极开拓海外市场。越南近年来则快速扩张钢铁产能，供应品类涵盖建筑用钢、热轧卷板、管材及镀锌板等。 进口回流已引发国内钢铁生产商的警觉。 美国钢铁企业9月已联名敦促特朗普政府对韩国钢铁出货量激增展开调查，指出建筑用钢、管材及平轧产品进口量均出现大幅上升。数据显示，仅9月一个月，韩国钢铁出货量即达51.9万吨，环比8月增长21%，来自日本的进口量同期亦跳升60%。 关税保护效力受限，国内产能扩张难解近渴 特朗普政府对外国钢铁征收的50%关税，原本旨在通过抬高进口成本来保护Nucor、Steel Dynamics及Cleveland-Cliffs等美国国内生产商。然而， 持续旺盛的需求已将美国国内价格推升至令外国供应商即便缴纳关税后仍有利可图的水平，关税的隔离效果因此大打折扣。 美国国内钢厂已随价格上涨加快生产。 据美国钢铁协会数据，截至11月14日当周，美国钢铁产量同比增长5.9%。然而，产量提升并未有效缓解供应紧张，钢厂停产事故、强劲的订单积压以及进口量下滑，共同制约了市场上可即时获取的钢铁数量。 Nucor首席执行官Leon Topalian在10月底的三季度业绩电话会议上表示，“进口量近月来持续增加，其中来自韩国的进口出现大幅激增。但毋庸置疑，需求非常健康。即便今年进口量有所攀升，美国国内出货量在过去三个季度中仍逐季上升。” 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 推动黄仁勋下台的“自媒体黑嘴”：由Anthropic的早期投资者资助
articles.summary: 黄仁勋于11月12日辞去英伟达CEO职务，英伟达董事会11月23日宣布将其复职，并在监管文件中援引美国政府高级官员的表态称其"不构成国家安全风险"。 在这一事件的舆论发酵过程中，研究人员Kevin Bass梳理出一条资金脉络：率先发文呼吁黄仁勋辞职的新闻简报《Transformer》，以及大篇幅跟进报道的新上线的播客节目《Machine Gods》，均指向同一个资助方—— Tarbell人工智能新闻中心 ，而Tarbell的核心金主，正是Facebook联合创始人、 Anthropic早期投资者Dustin Moskovitz 的慈善机构。 但Tarbell方面表示，其捐助者"对旗下记者或受资助媒体没有任何编辑控制权"，且目前没有任何资助记录可将具体资金与特定报道直接挂钩。 辞职前三天，《Transformer》率先喊话 11月9日，黄仁勋承认与Alice Huang存在婚外情的次日，简报《Transformer》编辑Shakeel Hashim发表文章，标题直接：《黄仁勋应该辞职》。 文章认为，黄仁勋将其与Alice Huang的往来描述为"正常关系"，是在误导员工、投资者和公众。三天后，黄仁勋宣布辞职。 《Transformer》是Tarbell旗下的自有刊物。 其官网伦理声明页面显示，该刊物"主要由Coefficient Giving（前身为Open Philanthropy）资助"——这正是Moskovitz与其妻Cari Tuna共同创立的慈善机构。该页面承诺在报道资助方相关内容时予以披露，英伟达并不在其资助方之列，上述呼吁辞职的文章也未附任何资金说明。 新上线播客《Machine Gods》：11集节目中有5集聚焦黄仁勋事件 10月5日，Tarbell宣布启动一项1000万美元的新闻资助计划，首批资金流向NPR：其中25万美元拨给NPR的"权力与影响"报道团队，48万美元拨给由前《Hard Fork》主持人Kevin Roose和Casey Newton联合制作的新播客《Machine Gods》。 该节目于10月21日上线，定位为"AI现实主义"。在截至11月20日的11集节目中，有5集聚焦黄仁勋事件，集中于11月4日至18日之间。 11月11日那集的宣传语称，节目将讨论"可能是冷战以来最重大的情报泄露事件"。在节目中，Roose更进一步表示："我认为这可能是冷战以来最重大的情报行动。"他同时提到，黄仁勋早在这段关系曝光之前就一直主张放宽出口管制。 同一集中，一位主持人甚至提前预判了黄仁勋的命运："我不认为他能挺过去，我认为他会辞职。"他还称，一套"对某国政府利益最大化"的芯片政策，看起来会和英伟达的政策非常相似。 黄仁勋次日辞职。数小时后，Roose录制了一段独白，开篇称黄仁勋的崛起是"美国资本主义史上最伟大的白手起家故事之一"，随即话锋一转："就在几小时前，黄仁勋以耻辱之身辞职。" 然而，就在这番"冷战"定性发出12天后，华尔街日报撤回了相关报道，承认Alice Huang与情报机构的关联可能仅属间接性质。 利益网络：顾问、资金与Anthropic的交集 11月18日那集节目邀请了Ben Buchanan，节目将其介绍为"最初芯片出口管制政策的设计者"。节目进行到一半时，播客《Machine Gods》主持人Newton主动披露： "你是Anthropic的顾问，我的未婚妻也在那里工作。" 在资金来源层面，Tarbell的支持者名单中，Coefficient Giving连续四年（2023年至2026年）位列最高捐助级别（终身捐款100万美元及以上）。据Fox News今年8月援引捐款数据库的报道，Coefficient已向Tarbell捐款逾470万美元。 Tarbell的另一主要支持者是Survival and Flourishing Fund，该基金由Skype联合创始人Jaan Tallinn创立—— Tallinn正是Anthropic2021年首轮融资的领投方。 资金链的核心逻辑 研究人员Bass的核心论点在于：Anthropic的表现越好，流入Tarbell等机构的资金池就越大。 Moskovitz与Tuna已于2025年初将其持有的Anthropic股份转入一家非营利机构。据《纽约时报》报道，在Anthropic上周以每股83美元完成IPO后，这笔股份目前价值数十亿美元。 与此同时，黄仁勋此前曾是AI风险论最直言不讳的批评者之一，而AI安全叙事正是Anthropic创始人Dario Amodei构建品牌的核心支柱。两人去年曾就出口管制和开源模型问题公开交锋。 尽管线索指向Anthropic，但目前没有任何资助记录可将具体资金与特定报道或节目集数直接挂钩；Tarbell明确声称其捐助者"对旗下记者或受资助媒体没有任何编辑控制权"；黄仁勋事件最初由《纽约时报》率先披露；Bass在相关报道中引用频率最高的分析人士，来自美国外交关系委员会。 黄仁勋预计将于下周出席国会听证。Tarbell表示，计划在2027年底前向新闻机构累计分发至少1000万美元。 articles.title: 1天20倍！上周五买入英伟达期权的买家火了，周一放话“开盘即卖，感谢老黄”
articles.summary: 一场押注英伟达反弹的期权交易，在周一早间因CEO黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）重新执掌帅印而迎来爆发式兑现。 据彭博11月25日报道，Reddit用户Outrageous-Voice1459以1.9万美元买入的英伟达看涨期权，单日暴涨逾1984%，净赚37.69万美元，其在社交媒体上高呼“开盘即卖，感谢老黄”的帖子迅速引发广泛关注。 英伟达股价周一单日飙升31%至165.05美元 ，此前该股本月累计跌幅已达39%。黄仁勋重返CEO职位的消息成为直接催化剂，令此前布局反弹的多头期权持仓集中兑现。 这场期权盛宴不止于散户。据彭博报道，一名机构交易员此前买入1月到期、行权价160美元的看涨期权，周一卖出其中一半仓位， 单笔锁定收益达2380万美元 。与此同时，股价大涨后，部分大型机构也开始建立对冲头寸，以防股价再度回落。 散户一战成名，“感谢老黄”刷屏WallStreetBets Reddit论坛r/WallStreetBets上，Outrageous-Voice1459晒出券商账户截图，称此次交易让自己“一笔赚到了年薪的10倍”，并留下那句广为流传的“SOLD AT OPEN. THANK YOU JENSEN”。 据彭博核实， 该用户的交易入场细节与同一时间、同一价格在电子期权交易所发生的一笔真实大宗交易记录相吻合 ，交易的真实性得到确认。 与此同时，社交媒体上另一笔“神操作”同样引发热议——据称有人买入周一到期、行权价160美元的看涨期权，并在大涨中获利颇丰。然而，据彭博对当日期权成交记录的核查， 该笔交易并无任何可查证的痕迹 。 期权研究机构VolSignals联合创始人Daniel Roos表示： “目前没有证据证明这笔交易真实发生过。即便确有其事，在指数或热门标的出现如此剧烈波动时，这类订单流也完全属于正常现象。” 机构早已布局，多策略押注反弹 散户的高光时刻背后，机构投资者的布局更为系统。据彭博报道，在英伟达股价持续下跌的过程中，部分期权交易员已悄然将看涨头寸移至更低的行权价，以更低成本换取更快兑现反弹收益的机会。 另有机构买入数以万计的看涨期权及看涨价差组合，押注英伟达股价在明年初前回升；还有交易员选择卖出看跌期权，愿意在股价进一步下跌时以约定价格接盘。 其中最具代表性的是那笔1月到期、行权价160美元的看涨期权 ——持有人在周一股价飙升至165.05美元后，卖出一半仓位，单笔锁定2380万美元收益。 随着英伟达股价周一单日急涨31%，市场情绪迅速从押注反弹切换至防范回调。据彭博报道，股价飙升后，部分大型交易员已开始建立新的对冲头寸，以应对股价可能再度下滑的风险。 这一动向表明，尽管黄仁勋回归提振了市场信心，但经历本月近四成跌幅后，机构对英伟达后市走势仍保持审慎， 多空博弈在新的价格区间内重新展开 。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
